summary: A 1934 CCC-built lookout cabin, originally at Camp Six Mountain, was dismantled and reassembled at Bear Basin Butte in the mid-1990s; it is now a Forest Service summer rental.

facts.status_note: Original structure stood at Camp Six (Upper Coon Mountain / Camp Six Mountain); moved to Bear Basin Butte and reassembled there.

access.note: Public by reservation on recreation.gov as part of the Bear Basin Lookout and Pierson Cabin rental; not open for casual visits.

visit.trail_note: High-clearance 4WD recommended; last half mile is steep gravel. Rented as a pair with Pierson Cabin (built 1990s in 1930s style); the cabin holds three double beds (one a bunk), the lookout itself has only a futon.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Smith River National Recreation Area, Six Rivers National Forest

events.note: An earlier, separate lookout was built on Bear Basin Butte itself in 1924.
That 1924 Bear Basin Butte lookout was struck by lightning and burned.
Camp Six Lookout built by a CCC crew on Upper Coon Mountain (NHLR). FFLOS instead dates first construction on the same site to 1923, with the current BC-301-plan cabin built later (year not given).
By the 1950s the Camp Six site had been taken over by electronic facilities and the lookout was decommissioned; exact year not given.
Restoration of the Camp Six lookout began, but vandalism followed before it was complete.
Recreation.gov listing dates the move of the lookout from Camp Six to Bear Basin Butte to 1996.
FFLOS instead dates the reassembly at Bear Basin Butte and entry into the recreation rental program to 1997; only the tower piers remain at the Camp Six site.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 6, 1999.

notes_for_editor: Two distinct prior structures are easy to conflate: (1) a 1924 lookout on Bear Basin Butte itself, burned 1936, unrelated to the current building; (2) the Camp Six/Upper Coon Mountain cabin (built 1934 per NHLR, or first built 1923 per FFLOS with an undated later replacement cabin) that was moved to Bear Basin Butte in 1996 (recreation.gov) or 1997 (FFLOS) and is the structure standing today. The tower record's own 'built: 1934' event matches NHLR but not FFLOS; left as-is since it's directly sourced. No corrections proposed to the tower record itself -- its fields (name, location, status 'relocated', agency) all check out against these sources. The FFLA CA list entry confirms 'Relocated' status and the NHLR US 288/CA 21 numbers; an adjacent table row for a different lookout (Basalt Hill, NHLR US 880/CA 90) sits right next to this one in the cached HTML and could be misread as a conflicting register number for Bear Basin Butte -- it is not, it belongs to the preceding row.
